finding: This round strengthened §4's fenced-command rule to name the interpreter, after §1's own block was found to print nothing under zsh. The rule's predicate is still "prints something", and §1's block defeats it one level up: it calls bare `tp`, so a `tp` on PATH older than `ground --units` makes it print a complete, well-formed table of zeros at exit 0. Measured — a stub `tp` on PATH that exits 2 on `--units`, running §1's own loop verbatim under `bash` over the last four tags: `0.36.0 0 28 / 0.37.0 0 19 / 1.0.0 0 15`, exit 0. The mechanism is that `tp ground ... 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^u[0-9]'` yields "0" on any failure and the `echo` fires regardless, so the block cannot distinguish an absent binary from a spec with no floor. (On this machine PATH `tp` is v1.0.0 and the block is honest; that is a property of the operator, not of the artifact.) The repository's own standing rule is that every tp call during self-development routes through the freshly-built binary. So the release's central derivation — the one that removed the floor-budget warning — is green under a rule it would fail if the rule measured what it is for.
